_meta.indication: AQNEURSA is indicated for the treatment of neurological manifestations of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) in adults and pediatric patients weighing >=15 kg.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial with two 12-week treatment periods.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with a confirmed diagnosis of NPC aged 5 to 67 years.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Applicant's prespecified primary endpoint was the modified Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (mSARA) total score at the end of each 12-week treatment period; approval was based on the FDA-recommended functional SARA (fSARA) reanalysis.
pivotal_trials.result: Estimated treatment difference for fSARA total score was -0.45 (95% CI: -0.70, -0.19), favoring levacetylleucine, p<0.001 (p=0.0009). Applicant's proposed primary mSARA difference was -0.96 (95% CI: -1.45, -0.46), p=0.0003.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5% and greater than placebo) are abdominal pain, dysphagia, upper respiratory tract infections, and vomiting. In Treatment Period I (AQNEURSA N=30, placebo N=30): upper respiratory tract infection 17% (5) vs 3% (1) placebo; abdominal pain 7% (2) vs 0%; dysphagia 7% (2) vs 0%; vomiting 7% (2) vs 0%.
target_moa: Levacetylleucine (N-acetyl-L-leucine) is a modified amino acid; its mechanism of action is unknown. It is metabolized into acetate and L-leucine; nonclinical data suggest it reduces lysosomal volume and glycosphingolipid accumulation in NPC models.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee was not held for this application; it did not raise challenging efficacy or safety issues that needed external input.

basis.text: Applicant requested breakthrough therapy designation in its IND submission received by FDA on January 7, 2019; FDA issued a breakthrough therapy designation request denied letter on March 5, 2019.

Following an evaluation of this request, the FDA issued a breakthrough therapy designation request denied letter on March 5, 2019.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation received September 8, 2021 for NALL (levacetylleucine) for NPC.

basis.text: Priority review granted because NPC is a serious condition with no approved treatments.

citations.quote: The Division determined the application would receive a priority review because NPC is a serious condition with no approved treatments.

summary.text: NDA 219132 was submitted via the 505(b)(1) pathway on January 24, 2024 and granted priority review because NPC is a serious condition with no approved treatments; the drug had orphan drug designation for NPC (granted September 8, 2021). A breakthrough therapy designation request was denied. Approval was traditional, based on one adequate and well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence.

citations.quote: The Applicant submitted NDA 219132 for levacetylleucine, a new molecular entity, for the treatment of NPC via the 505(b)(1) regulatory pathway on January 24, 2024.
The Division determined the application would receive a priority review because NPC is a serious condition with no approved treatments.
On September 8, 2021, the Applicant received an orphan drug designation for NALL for NPC.
the FDA issued a breakthrough therapy designation request denied letter on March 5, 2019.
Substantial evidence of effectiveness of levacetylleucine for NPC was established using data from one adequate and well-controlled trial and confirmatory evidence (CE).
